short: Bioinspired Spiky Peroxidase-Mimics for Localized Bacterial
title: Bioinspired Spiky Peroxidase-Mimics for Localized Bacterial Capture and Synergistic Catalytic Sterilization

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Bacterial wound infection needs an antibiotic-free agent that eradicates bacteria at ultralow dose. A virus-like spiky shell on a cascaded Cu(II)+MoO3 peroxidase-mimic should capture bacteria and kill them by localized ROS.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (HYP/need), s2 (HYP/hypothesis), s3 (DES/base_system), s4 (DES/modification), s5 (DES/architecture), s6 (PRC/synthesis), s7 (PRC/deposition). Premises: Mo/W transition-metal compounds are reported to bind H2O2 strongly and to lower the reaction barrier; Viruses carry surface spikes that let them attach to and enter host cells

states.title: Structure state
states.head: V-POD-M keeps the octahedral core of POD-M but its whole surface carries dense mesoporous spikes, where POD-M is smooth. A continuous silica shell about 130 nm thick covers the V-POD-M core.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Cu(II) and MoO3 together turn H2O2 into hydroxyl radicals far faster than either centre alone. MoO3 binds H2O2 into a peroxo-complex intermediate that lowers the Fenton-like barrier at Cu, accelerating .OH release.
states.detail: Absorbed: s11 (PRP/value), s12 (MEC/pathway), s13 (PRP/value), s14 (MEC/pathway), s15 (PRP/value)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: In S. aureus-infected rabbit wounds, V-POD-M+H2O2 closes the wound by day 16 as well as vancomycin does.

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: A bioinspired spiky peroxidase-mimic sterilizes by localized capture and catalysis, working antibiotic-free at ultralow dose

nodes.title: MICRO, F1
nodes.head: POD-M is a smooth-faced octahedron about 2 um across; V-POD-M keeps that core and is covered with fine mesoporous spikes
nodes.solves: V-POD-M keeps the octahedral core of POD-M but its whole surface carries dense mesoporous spikes, where POD-M is smooth
nodes.note: F1c/c-1 (POD-M) show flat facets with the printed label 'Smooth surface'; F1d/d-1 (V-POD-M) show a hairy rim with 'mesoporous spike' arrows. F1 is tier C2 and offers no panel crops, so the whole figure was read. F1c-1 also shows loose dark debris labelled 'unstable MOF'.

nodes.title: EDS:spectrum, F1
nodes.head: C, O, Cu and Mo fill the whole particle in both POD-M and V-POD-M EDX maps
nodes.solves: Cu and Mo catalytic centres are distributed homogeneously through the POD-M core in both samples
nodes.note: Cu (magenta) and Mo (yellow) tiles of F1e and F1f are uniformly filled with no core-shell contrast; in F1f they stop inside the Si rim.

nodes.title: MICRO, F5
nodes.head: With POD-M+H2O2 the bacteria sit in clusters away from the particles, while with V-POD-M+H2O2 every bacterium is embedded in the particle aggregate. After V-POD-M+H2O2 the bacterial envelopes are broken and the cytoplasm granular, where after V-POD-M alone the envelope is continuous
nodes.solves: Localized capture-killing: the spikes hold the bacterium against the particle so the .OH burst is delivered in situ at its membrane
nodes.note: Same reading for both strains; the V-POD-M panels are false-coloured (bacteria yellow, particles grey). The spike penetration of the cytomembrane claimed in the linked text is not resolved: at the blue 'Bacterial capture' arrows the dark spiky material lies against the envelope, not visibly inside it. In F5c the membrane damage is a surface dent rather than a collapse of the cell.
nodes.necessity_reason: s14 keeps shown support from o13 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F4
nodes.head: With V-POD-M+H2O2 the bacteria are all red and gathered into one dense captured patch, where controls are green and evenly scattered
nodes.solves: Localized capture-killing: the spikes hold the bacterium against the particle so the .OH burst is delivered in situ at its membrane
nodes.note: F4 is tier C3 and offers no panel crops, so the whole figure was read. The POD-M+H2O2 fields are also almost entirely red, only sparser, so the linked text's 'insufficient capability to eradicate' is not what F4d shows; the dashed 'Capture' outline marks the clustered region.
nodes.necessity_reason: s14 keeps shown support from o11 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F5
nodes.head: After H2O2 the POD-M octahedra are gone and only crumpled sheets remain, an alternative reason for the weak killing that the text never weighs
nodes.solves: V-POD-M+H2O2 reduces S. aureus and E. coli to zero colonies, where POD-M+H2O2 leaves 45-58 CFU
nodes.note: Both POD-M+H2O2 panels show flat torn foils with no facets left; the V-POD-M+H2O2 particles keep their bulk.

nodes.title: ATOM, F6
nodes.head: The flat slab still rests on the bilayer at 24 ns, while the spiky tube has passed through it by 16 ns and splayed the lipid tails
nodes.solves: A spiky surface pierces and binds the lipid bilayer far more strongly than a flat surface
nodes.note: The two rows are not rendered alike: the bilayer of F6b is already drawn in a looser licorice style at 0 ns, so part of the apparent disorder is a rendering difference. A pulling force is applied to both surfaces, so penetration is force-driven, not spontaneous.
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and s13 keeps shown support from o10.

nodes.title: PL, F2
nodes.head: The oxTMB band near 652 nm appears only for TMB+H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 (A about 0.60); the other three traces stay below 0.1. The TAOH emission band peaks near 420 nm and is tallest for TA+H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 (about 480 a.u.) against about 190 a.u.
nodes.solves: Cu(II) and MoO3 together turn H2O2 into hydroxyl radicals far faster than either centre alone
nodes.note: Peak of the purple trace reads about 0.60 at 650-655 nm; the red Cu(II) trace has a shallow bump near 0.08. The band maximum sits at about 420 nm, not the 435 nm quoted in the F2d caption. Cu(II) alone about 275 a.u., MoO3 alone about 220 a.u. The intensity axis carries no scale, so the sixfold factor quoted in the linked text cannot be checked from the panel; only the ordering is readable. DMPOX and DMPO-C marks sit between the DMPO-OH lines in both active traces. Blank 185, Cu(II) 240, MoO3 195, Cu(II)+MoO3 380 a.u., against the linked text's 'only the TA+H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 mixture shows an intense photoluminescence signal'.
nodes.detail: o4: The oxTMB band near 652 nm appears only for TMB+H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 (A about 0.60); the other three traces stay below 0.1; o5: The TAOH emission band peaks near 420 nm and is tallest for TA+H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 (about 480 a.u.) against about 190 a.u. for TA+H2O2; o6: The four-line DMPO-OH signal is several times taller for H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 than for H2O2+Cu(II), and flat for H2O2 and H2O2+MoO3; a2: All four TA groups give 185-380 a.u. of TAOH fluorescence, so the Cu(II)+MoO3 gain is about twofold over the blank, not an on/off signal
nodes.inner_audit: a2: Blank 185, Cu(II) 240, MoO3 195, Cu(II)+MoO3 380 a.u., against the linked text's 'only the TA+H2O2+Cu(II)+MoO3 mixture shows an intense photoluminescence signal'.

nodes.title: evidence, F2, F3
nodes.head: H2O2 adsorption on MoO3 crosses a 0.06 eV barrier and the MoO2(O2) peroxo intermediate lies 0.78 eV below the reactants. With the peroxo intermediate both barriers are 0.24 eV, against 0.38 and 0.36 eV for direct Cu/H2O2, and the path ends 0.35 eV lower.
nodes.solves: MoO3 binds H2O2 into a peroxo-complex intermediate that lowers the Fenton-like barrier at Cu, accelerating .OH release
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: Printed levels 0.00, 0.06 and -0.78 eV on the diagram; matches the linked text. Path 1 (red) 0.00, 0.24, -0.67, -0.85, -0.61, -1.42 eV; Path 2 (blue) 0.00, 0.38, -0.49, -0.72, -0.36, -1.07 eV. Second barriers: 0.24 eV (red) vs 0.36 eV (blue). Error bars on the MoO3 bar are small and it is clearly separated from the blank, against the linked text's 'no peroxide catalytic activity of MoO3'.
nodes.detail: o7: H2O2 adsorption on MoO3 crosses a 0.06 eV barrier and the MoO2(O2) peroxo intermediate lies 0.78 eV below the reactants; o8: With the peroxo intermediate both barriers are 0.24 eV, against 0.38 and 0.36 eV for direct Cu/H2O2, and the path ends 0.35 eV lower; a1: MoO3 alone gives absorbance 0.055 against 0.017 for H2O2 alone and 0.082 for Cu(II) alone, so MoO3 by itself does oxidize TMB
nodes.inner_audit: a1: Error bars on the MoO3 bar are small and it is clearly separated from the blank, against the linked text's 'no peroxide catalytic activity of MoO3'.

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: The flat surface plateaus at 4.3 nm and -3000 kJ/mol after about 6 ns, while the spiky surface keeps closing to 1.0 nm and gaining to about -7000 kJ/mol at 24 ns
nodes.solves: A spiky surface pierces and binds the lipid bilayer far more strongly than a flat surface
nodes.note: At 15 ns the spiky energy curve reads about -6.2e3 kJ/mol where the linked text says about -6500; the flat plateau starts near 6 ns where the text says 5 ns. Neither spiky curve has reached a plateau at 24 ns.
nodes.detail: o10: The flat surface plateaus at 4.3 nm and -3000 kJ/mol after about 6 ns, while the spiky surface keeps closing to 1.0 nm and gaining to about -7000 kJ/mol at 24 ns
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for s13 (o10).

nodes.title: ASSAY, F4
nodes.head: Colony counts fall from 819 and 971 CFU to 0 for V-POD-M+H2O2 and to 45 and 58 CFU for POD-M+H2O2. V-POD-M+H2O2 has the lowest MIC of the four groups, near 16 ug/mL for S.
nodes.solves: V-POD-M+H2O2 reduces S. aureus and E. coli to zero colonies, where POD-M+H2O2 leaves 45-58 CFU
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: V-POD-M alone gives 496 and 602 CFU against 673 and 757 for POD-M alone. The OD600 curves of F4b,c stay flat for both +H2O2 groups over 12 h and confirm the same ranking. The concentration axis is broken before 510 ug/mL, so the arrow positions are hard to read exactly; in F4f the V-POD-M+H2O2 arrow sits well above 16 ug/mL on the axis although the linked text quotes 16 ug/mL for both strains.
nodes.detail: o14: Colony counts fall from 819 and 971 CFU to 0 for V-POD-M+H2O2 and to 45 and 58 CFU for POD-M+H2O2; o15: V-POD-M+H2O2 has the lowest MIC of the four groups, near 16 ug/mL for S. aureus, where V-POD-M alone needs above 250 ug/mL
nodes.necessity_reason: s15 keeps shown support from a3 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F7, F8
nodes.head: Control and H2O2 sections are packed with dense inflammatory nuclei, while V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin sections show ordered collagen like normal skin. The Masson epidermal band between the dashed lines is thick and uneven in control and H2O2 and thin and regular in V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin
nodes.solves: In S. aureus-infected rabbit wounds, V-POD-M+H2O2 closes the wound by day 16 as well as vancomycin does
nodes.op: compare across conditions, measure feature metric
nodes.note: Red dashed boxes mark the infiltrated zones in the two failing groups; green arrows mark fibroblasts and vessels in the two healed groups. At the 50 um scale the band edges are only roughly resolved and the POD-M+H2O2 section is cut obliquely, so the ranking is clear but the thickness is not measurable from this panel.
nodes.necessity_reason: s16, s17 keeps shown support from o16, o17, a4, o20 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F7
nodes.head: Control and H2O2 wounds grow to about 300 mm2 by day 8 and are still about 160 mm2 at day 16, while V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin fall to 12-15 mm2. At day 16 the V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin wounds are closed pink scars while control and H2O2 wounds are still open and crusted.
nodes.solves: In S. aureus-infected rabbit wounds, V-POD-M+H2O2 closes the wound by day 16 as well as vancomycin does
nodes.note: Day 0 about 128 mm2 for all four arms; the V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin curves lie on top of each other from day 8 onward. Both treated rows pass through a dark scab at day 4; a ruler in every frame gives the scale. Against the linked text's 'the wounds present no expansion tendency and are completely repaired within 15 d'; the curve is still above zero at day 16 and sits at about 190 mm2 on day 4.
nodes.detail: o16: Control and H2O2 wounds grow to about 300 mm2 by day 8 and are still about 160 mm2 at day 16, while V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin fall to 12-15 mm2; o17: At day 16 the V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin wounds are closed pink scars while control and H2O2 wounds are still open and crusted; a4: The V-POD-M+H2O2 wound still expands from about 128 to about 197 mm2 by day 1 and measures about 12 mm2 at day 16
nodes.inner_audit: a4: Against the linked text's 'the wounds present no expansion tendency and are completely repaired within 15 d'; the curve is still above zero at day 16 and sits at about 190 mm2 on day 4.

nodes.note: Bar heights match the values quoted in the linked text; the *** bracket spans control against both V-POD-M+H2O2 and vancomycin.
